newsitem.title: INDIA: BETTER INDIA CORPORATE PROFITS IN 2ND HALF - KOTHARI.
newsitem.headline: BETTER INDIA CORPORATE PROFITS IN 2ND HALF - KOTHARI.

text.p: Major Indian companies are expected to show improved second half profits in financial year 1997/98 (April-March), Kothari Pioneer Asset Management Company Ltd said.

"Large corporates are expected to post better bottomlines in the second half of the current year on account of good monsoon, improved demand in core sectors, easing of liquidity and fall in interest rates and reduction in corporate taxes," Kothari said in its annual investment review obtained by Reuters on Monday.
Kothari AMC is the Indian affiliate of Pioneer Group of the United States.
Indian stock markets were emerging from a prolonged bear phase and large capitalised stocks normally led the up trend, Kothari said.
"Based on forward valuations, large-cap stocks still appear to offer scope for appreciation despite the recent run-up in prices."
"While the large-cap story may currently appear overdone, long term investors are safer in this sector as it offers quality exposure to the Indian market," Kothari added.
Large-capitalised stocks have been market outperformers in the 45 percent rally seen in the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share index in calendar year 1997, analysts said.
"Also, there may be short term underperformance of this sector...however, in the longer term, large-cap stocks should do well," Kothari said.
The Bombay index last week surged to a 34-month high just shy of 4,653.31 -- an all-time high set on September 12, 1994 but later fell due to heavy profit-taking.
On Monday, the index rallied 83.76 points, or 1.90 percent, to end at 4,481.30 at the start of the weekly account.
